newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-BACK SPASMS OUST SELES FROM NEW JERSEY TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BACK SPASMS OUST SELES FROM NEW JERSEY TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Monica Seles, suffering from back spasms through most of the match, quit in the second set of the semifinals of the A&P Women's Tennis Classic on Saturday, allowing Chandra Rubin to advance to the finals.

Rubin, ranked 29, won 3-6 3-2 and will play 16-year-old Anna Kournikova of Russia in the championship match. Kournikova, who reached the semifinals at Wimbledon before Losing to Martina Hingis, beat Maggie Maleeva of Bulgaria 6-4 6-1 on Saturday.

"I was in pain from the beginning of the match and it got worse despite the treatment," Seles said. Seles, ranked third in the world, received massages to her mid-back on three visits to courtside by the tournament trainer.

"The problem started (on Friday) during the quarterfinal when we had such a long rain delay," Seles said. "I didn't stretch enough in my warmup (on Saturday). The muscles in my back were tightening and I though t it was safer to stop before it got any worse."
Seles has been plagued with injuries since returning to the tour two years ago after a 28-month layoff following an on-court stabbing in Hamburg, Germany.
Last year at the Australian Open, Seles injured her left shoulder in her run to the only Grand Slam title she has earned in her comeback. She has won nine Grand Slams.
"If this had been the last Trournament of the year, I would have played," said the 23-year-old lefthander, "but I want to make sure that I am ready this summer and able to compete at the U.S. Open."
Rubin said she was not aware of Seles' pain "because she was moving well and playing hard. It was unfortunate the way it ended, but I hope I would have won anyway."
